title: 〜たい — I want to…
pattern: verb (ます form without ます) + たい
explanation: To say you want to do something, take the ます form, drop ます and add たい: {行|い}きます → {行|い}きたい — I want to go. たい then works like an い-adjective: {行|い}きたいです (polite), {行|い}きたくない (don’t want to), {行|い}きたかった (wanted to).
natural: Talking about your own wishes: いつか{日本|にほん}に{住|す}みたい — I’d like to live in Japan one day. With food and drink, を often becomes が: お{寿司|すし}が{食|た}べたい.
stiff: Asking someone above you {何|なに}が{食|た}べたいですか can sound too direct. An offer is softer: {何|なに}か{飲|の}みませんか (the next lesson). And for wanting a thing rather than an action, it’s ほしい: {水|みず}がほしい.

examples.japanese: いつか日本に行きたいです。
examples.furigana: いつか{日本|にほん}に{行|い}きたいです。
examples.english: I want to go to Japan one day.

gap.before: いつか{日本|にほん}に{行|い}き
gap.why: Want to: drop ます, add たい.

examples.furigana: {今日|きょう}は{家|いえ}で{休|やす}みたい。
examples.english: Today I want to rest at home.

gap.before: {今日|きょう}は{家|いえ}で{休|やす}み
gap.why: Want to rest: 休みたい.

examples.japanese: 寒いから、出かけたくない。
examples.furigana: {寒|さむ}いから、{出|で}かけたくない。
examples.english: It’s cold, so I don’t want to go out.

gap.why: Don’t want to: たい → たくない, like an い-adjective.

examples.japanese: 晩ご飯は何が食べたい？
examples.furigana: {晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}は{何|なに}が{食|た}べたい？
examples.english: What do you want for dinner?

gap.before: {晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}は{何|なに}が{食|た}べ
gap.why: Want to eat: 食べたい.
